source.title: Pushing the Efficiency Limit Using Structured Sparse Convolutions
source.authors: V. Verma; Nikhil Mehta; Shi-Jing Si; Ricardo Henao; L. Carin

record.tranche_reason: The study compares test accuracy and a filter-correlation measure across sparse convolution architectures and baselines; these results bear on measured network properties and generalization, using a different method from the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports classification accuracy, filter correlation, low-data robustness, and transfer results. Its statements about standard overparameterized networks generalizing well and cited lottery-ticket or pruning results are background, not rows. No result directly tests the listed versions about random-label memorization, width, convolution versus fully connected models, optimizer, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates sparse convolution design, filter correlation, limited-data accuracy and transfer performance. None measures V1–V8: there is no random-label experiment, width sweep, fully connected comparator, optimizer or batch-size comparison, dropout intervention, magnitude-aware sharpness measure, or removal of memorized examples. Generalization and overparameterization appear as background motivations.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that SSC reduces parameters and theoretical computation from initialization, achieves competitive classification performance, lowers filter correlation, and improves limited-data and transfer performance in their experiments. Their conclusion also acknowledges limited practical speedup with existing deep-learning libraries.
record.recipe_differences: The study designs structured sparse convolution filters and compares their classification accuracy and correlation properties; it does not use the mapped versions' interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-data fraction changes the reported overfitting-robustness difference; the difference becomes more significant as training data decreases. The transfer comparison uses 100 Tiny-ImageNet classes.

fits_no_version.finding: SSC has lower filter correlation than standard convolution in 31 of 33 layers; the prose reports a grouped 21-layer advantage over explicit orthogonality constraints.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured sparse convolutions can reduce filter correlation relative to standard and explicitly regularized convolutional filters.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report better limited-data accuracy for SSC than standard convolution, with a larger advantage as training data decreases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SSC can improve ResNet-32 classification accuracy when CIFAR-10 training data is limited.

fits_no_version.finding: SSC architectures selected on CIFAR-100 reportedly outperform GraSP networks transferred to a 100-class Tiny-ImageNet task at 90% and 95% sparsity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SSC's sparse architecture can transfer better than GraSP-derived sparsity in the tested setting.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
record.problems: The low-data robustness and transfer accuracy values are presented in figures without numeric values in the supplied text. The prose gives directional comparisons, and no uncertainty is stated for these results. The filter-correlation comparison reports layer counts but not per-layer numeric values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Classification benchmark accuracy compares sparse pruning methods and model compression performance, but does not measure the claim's mapped behaviors or gap-related properties.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of learned local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove penalties.
Dropout effects, including small-data, underfitting and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized training examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures fit no listed version; this does not negate the reported SSC findings. The classification benchmark results omitted by the reader are explicitly declared in rows_left_out and do not supply missing evidence for these versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolution versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Large-batch generalization gap and recipe adaptation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-32 with SSC filters
rows.size_stated: 10% of the total parameters in a standard ResNet-32 architecture
rows.operation_detail: Average absolute filter correlation across layers after training on CIFAR-100.
rows.measure: Average absolute pairwise filter correlation; SSC lower than standard filters in 31 of 33 layers.
rows.value: SSC filters have lower correlation measure for 31 layers out of 33
rows.note: The paper frames lower correlation as fewer redundant filters; this is not one of the mapped version measures.
rows.check: The reported 31-of-33-layer comparison is supported, but filter correlation does not measure any listed version, including V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: ResNet-32 with soft-orthogonality constraints
rows.operation_detail: Compare average absolute filter correlation by layer with SSC filters.
rows.measure: Average absolute pairwise filter correlation; SSC is lower in 21 layers than methods with explicit regularization constraints.
rows.value: SSC filters have lower correlation measure for 21 layers
rows.note: The prose groups the explicit-regularization comparison and does not separate soft and double-soft orthogonality values.
rows.check: Method-comparison result outside V1–V8. The subject is SO, but the value describes SSC relative to regularized baselines. The prose does not establish a separate 21-layer count for SO; consolidate with R3 unless Figure 3 resolves the comparisons.
